# The Entity Revolution: Why LLMs Are Killing Traditional Keyword SEO and What Marketers Must Do in 2025

## Introduction

We’re standing at a fast-moving inflection point in search. For the past two decades, SEO has been a discipline built around keywords, links and technical tweaks designed to win positions on search engine results pages (SERPs). In 2025, that framework is being upended by large language models (LLMs) and AI-powered search overviews that prioritize concise, entity-aware answers over link lists. This isn’t incremental change — it’s a structural shift in how people ask questions, how answers are assembled, and how attention flows across the web.

The data is stark and unavoidable. Market intelligence shows 5.6% of U.S. desktop search traffic now goes to AI-powered LLMs like ChatGPT and Perplexity. Google’s own landscape is changing: 58.5% of searches end up as “zero-click” queries, and AI Overviews from Google and competitors have reduced organic click-through rates by an estimated 20–40%. Even when search volume rose 21.6% from 2023 to 2024, clicks to external pages didn’t follow — users are finding answers inside AI responses instead of clicking through. ChatGPT processes about 37.5 million prompts per day versus Google’s roughly 14 billion searches, and that changing pattern of consumption is eroding traffic for top-ranking pages (some lose up to 45% of traffic when AI Overviews are present).

This trend matters if you work in generative engine optimisation, AI search optimization, ChatGPT SEO or entity based SEO. It forces a rethink of what “ranking” means: LLMs don’t rank pages the way Google’s classic algorithm did; they identify and synthesize entities, relationships and authoritative signals to produce answers. In this article — a trend analysis for the generative engine optimisation audience — I’ll map the mechanics of the shift, highlight the key components you must master, offer concrete, tactical applications, and outline the strategic moves that will keep you visible in a future where LLMs shape discovery.

Expect citations, numbers, vendor names (Google, OpenAI/ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, Gemini, Datos, Semrush, Ahrefs, HubSpot), and actionable takeaways. This is not about abandoning SEO — it’s about evolving it into entity-first, context-aware optimization that wins in the LLM era.

## Understanding the Entity Revolution

"Entity" is no longer just a semantic SEO buzzword. At its core, an entity is a discrete thing: a person, organization, product, concept, event, or place — with attributes and relationships. LLMs and modern search stacks treat entities as the building blocks of answers. Instead of matching keywords, they map intent to entities and synthesize information from multiple sources to form coherent responses. That means users often receive a complete answer without ever visiting the original web pages — causing the rise in zero-click searches.

Why this matters now: LLMs can produce direct answers, overviews, and summaries by combining signals from the web, structured knowledge graphs, and proprietary datasets. Google’s AI Overviews aim to do exactly that: serve succinct, authoritative responses on the results page. Perplexity and ChatGPT (and models like Claude and Gemini) also generate conversational answers that users prefer for quick, pragmatic queries. Patrick Coffee wrote in the Wall Street Journal that “Chatbots are becoming the go-to source for online answers for many consumers, chipping away at the dominance of traditional web search.” That quote captures the behavioral tilt — users increasingly favor conversational, synthesized answers.

The statistics support this behavioral shift. Datos finds AI platforms now capture 5.6% of U.S. desktop search traffic. HubSpot reports 19% of marketers plan to add LLM SEO practices in 2025. Semrush and Ahrefs have documented traffic erosions: AI Overviews reduce organic CTR by 20–40%, and in some verticals the presence of AI-overview features can shave as much as 45% off traffic to top-ranked pages. Even more striking: Google’s search volume grew 21.6% from 2023 to 2024, yet clicks outward to publisher sites are flat or declining — showing search volume alone is no longer a proxy for site traffic.

Put simply: search queries are being resolved without clicks, and the resolution mechanism is entity synthesis. For marketers, this breaks the linear keyword-to-traffic pipeline built over years. Keywords still matter — queries are still inputs — but their function shifts from a direct path to traffic toward signals that help LLMs connect to the right entities and authoritative sources. Success metrics must evolve too: instead of pure rank and organic CTR, we now measure brand mentions inside AI outputs, accuracy of citations, and relationships between entities in knowledge graphs.

Understanding this shift is the first step. LLMs do three key things that degrade traditional keyword SEO effectiveness: (1) they surface synthesized answers rather than link lists; (2) they prioritize entity-level authority and relationships; and (3) they increasingly act as the first, and sometimes only, touchpoint in the user journey. That triad is the engine driving the entity revolution.

## Key Components and Analysis

To navigate this new ecosystem, marketers must understand the building blocks of LLM-driven discovery and how they differ from classic SEO. Below are the core components redefining visibility and ranking in 2025.

1. Entity Knowledge and Graphs
LLMs rely on structured and semi-structured knowledge about entities — profiles, attributes, canonical identifiers, and relationships. Google’s Knowledge Graph remains influential, but LLMs also draw on public and proprietary corpora. The better an entity is represented (consistent names, attributes, disambiguation), the more likely an LLM will reference it when synthesizing answers. This is why brand mentions, schema markup, and authoritative citations matter now more than ever.

2. Contextual and Intent Modeling
Keywords are context-poor. LLMs excel at modeling context and mapping it to intent. Query formulations that previously required SEO keyword matching are now interpreted as intentions that point to entities. For example, “best email platform for small e-commerce stores” is less about matching “email marketing tools” and more about mapping attributes (budget, integrations, ease-of-use) to relevant vendor entities and outcomes.

3. Citation and Source Attribution Mechanics
AI responses often include citations or sources. The mechanics of what gets cited — freshness, domain authority, topical relevance, unique data — are evolving priorities. Semrush predicts AI platforms may generate more traffic than traditional search by 2028, but that will depend heavily on how reliably AI can attribute and link back to original sources. Brands that get cited accurately in AI answers will retain visibility even if clicks drop.

4. Conversational and Follow-up Intent
LLMs enable multi-turn conversations. Each follow-up can shift intent, which means content must be modular, entity-rich and ready to be stitched into answers. Bite-sized, authoritative content blocks that an LLM can quote or summarize will perform better than long, keyword-optimized pages that don’t clearly delineate facts and entities.

5. Cross-Platform Aggregation (Google, ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, Gemini)
No single platform will own the entire discovery stack. Users split between Google’s AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Perplexity, emerging Claude/Gemini apps and vertical LLM tools. Datos’ number — 5.6% of desktop traffic to LLMs — is an early signal; adoption will vary by cohort and vertical. Ahrefs and Semrush data show that when AI Overviews appear in SERPs, organic CTRs fall 20–40% and top pages can lose up to 45% of traffic. That’s real, measurable impact.

6. New Measurement Signals
Rankings are now supplemented by new metrics: frequency of entity mentions in AI outputs, citation accuracy rates, volume of AI-driven referrals, and brand authority as perceived by models. HubSpot’s finding that 19% of marketers plan to adopt LLM SEO practices in 2025 highlights a pivot toward measuring these non-traditional KPIs.

7. Data Freshness and Unique Value
LLMs reward unique insights and freshness. If a model can answer a query using multiple sources, the standout will be the source with unique, verifiable data or an authoritative voice. This is why original research, proprietary datasets, and structured data will be competitive differentiators.

Analysis: The combined effect of these components is erosion of the keyword-as-king mindset. Where keywords signaled topical relevance, entities and relationships now signal authority and trustworthiness. The brands that win will be those that become well-modeled, well-cited entities in the datasets LLMs consume.

## Practical Applications

If you’re working in generative engine optimisation, this is where the rubber meets the road. Below are actionable tactics for adapting your SEO program to LLM-dominated discovery.

1. Build and Harden Your Entity Profile
- Create canonical, structured representations of your brand, products, and major people (use schema.org, JSON-LD).
- Maintain consistent NAP (name, address, phone) and business descriptions across authoritative directories and your site.
- Publish entity-specific pages that act as canonical sources: product hubs, executive bios, data pages, and FAQs.

2. Optimize for AI-Friendly Fragments
- Structure content into modular, factual blocks that LLMs can extract or summarize: short definitions, benefit lists, how-to steps, and comparative matrices.
- Use clear headings and schema to label facts (e.g., ProductFeature, Review, AggregateRating).

3. Prioritize Unique Data and Research
- Invest in original studies, data visualizations, and proprietary benchmarks. LLMs prefer unique facts they can attribute.
- Produce datasets and publish them in machine-readable formats (CSV, JSON-LD) to increase the chance of being cited.

4. Map Content to Intentual Entity Relationships
- Move beyond keyword mapping to intent-to-entity mapping. For each user intent, list the entities that answer it and craft content that highlights those relationships (e.g., “X integrates with Y to solve Z”).
- Create “entity pages” that explain relationships (partner integrations, use cases, case studies).

5. Optimize for Citation and Attribution
- Ensure your content includes clear citations, timestamps, and verifiable sources so AI systems can attribute correctly.
- Use canonical URLs, persistent identifiers (DOIs for research), and stable page structures.

6. Monitor AI Mentions and AI Referral Signals
- Track the presence of your brand or entity in AI outputs using tools that monitor mentions in ChatGPT-like responses and AI overviews.
- Create dashboards for new KPIs: AI mention frequency, citation accuracy rate, and AI referral volume.

7. Prepare for Conversational Journeys
- Create content that answers first-touch, follow-up, and deep-dive questions in modular form.
- Design content flows that anticipate multi-turn queries: summary+expandable details pattern.

8. Diversify Discovery Channels
- Optimize for multiple platforms: Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, Gemini, and vertical LLM apps.
- Build platform-specific strategies; for example, produce short, authoritative Q&A snippets for ChatGPT-style outputs and structured data for Google’s Knowledge Graph.

Actionable takeaway checklist (quick):
- Publish canonical JSON-LD for all major entities.
- Produce at least one piece of original data or research per quarter.
- Break top-traffic pages into extractable fact blocks.
- Add “citation metadata” (author, date, source) to every page.
- Set up AI-mention monitoring and a dashboard for AI KPIs.

## Challenges and Solutions

Transitioning from keyword SEO to entity-based, LLM-aware optimization introduces new challenges. Below I outline the most pressing ones and practical solutions.

Challenge 1: Measurement ambiguity — classic SEO metrics decline
Solution:
- Evolve KPIs to include AI-specific signals (AI mention frequency, citation accuracy, AI-driven conversions).
- Tie AI outputs to business outcomes: create attribution models that consider AI impressions as assisted channels (e.g., assisted conversions, brand lift).
- Use controlled experiments (A/B content published with different structures) to measure impact on AI citations.

Challenge 2: Volatile traffic — AI Overviews reduce organic CTR by 20–40%
Solution:
- Diversify value capture — focus on conversion-worthy assets (tools, gated content, product pages) rather than purely informational pages.
- Prioritize direct response content where a click is likely (interactive tools, calculators, trial offers).
- Use schema and clear CTAs in answerable fragments to encourage follow-through.

Challenge 3: Authority and citation misattribution
Solution:
- Harden your data: publish authoritative, verifiable sources and make them discoverable in machine-readable formats.
- Use persistent identifiers (DOIs, stable URLs) and make sure your citation metadata is correct.
- Proactively claim and optimize your presence on authoritative platforms and publisher networks that AI crawlers index.

Challenge 4: Platform fragmentation (Google vs ChatGPT vs Perplexity)
Solution:
- Treat platform differences as channel segmentation. Build a small test matrix to publish variants optimized for each major LLM or overview approach.
- Invest in cross-platform monitoring and adapt content based on which platforms cite you most frequently.

Challenge 5: Resource shift — need for data, schema, and technical integration
Solution:
- Cross-train teams: combine SEO, content, product, and data teams for entity governance.
- Prioritize engineering effort on schema, APIs, and machine-readable exports of data.
- Start small: pick high-value entity classes (products, pricing, case studies) and model them first.

Challenge 6: Maintaining editorial voice when answers are synthesized
Solution:
- Create signature content formats that LLMs are more likely to reference (original frameworks, branded research, unique templates).
- Encourage journalists and subject-matter experts on your team to produce authoritative explainers that are clear, concise, and citable.

A critical point: early adopters benefit. HubSpot reports 19% of marketers plan to add LLM SEO practices in 2025 — that means the majority are still catching up. Invest now to secure entity authority before citation patterns harden.

## Future Outlook

What does the next 3–5 years look like for search and discovery? The trajectory is clear: hybrid search paradigms will coexist, with LLM-powered answers growing in prominence and traditional link-based SERPs continuing to matter for specific intents. Industry forecasts — including Semrush’s projection that AI platforms may generate more traffic than traditional search by 2028 — suggest the balance will continue shifting toward AI-driven discovery.

Here are the most likely developments:

1. More Zero-Click Answers, but New Value Capture Models
Zero-click metrics will remain high for informational queries. But new value capture models will emerge: branded entities that are consistently cited by LLMs will enjoy indirect benefits (brand awareness, better-qualified leads, increased conversions through assisted channels). Organizations that convert AI mentions into micro-conversions (newsletter signups, tool usage, product trials) will claim value even without direct organic clicks.

2. Institutionalization of Entity Governance
Brands will set up entity governance teams — cross-functional groups that manage canonical data, schema implementations, and relationships to partners and content. Think “knowledge graph ops” sitting alongside SEO and content teams.

3. Platform Co-opetition and Standards
As AI platforms vie for trust, we’ll see increased demand for citation standards, verifiable data marks, and possibly a “provenance” protocol that tags facts with source attestations. This could be industry- or consortium-led, involving publishers and platforms.

4. AI Overviews Mature — Attribution Matters
If AI overviews start routing more referral-like traffic or provide richer, repeatable citations, publishers with high-quality, machine-readable data will retain influence. The organizations that invest in data cleanliness, persistent links, and unique value will be prioritized by models.

5. New Tools for LLM Content Ranking and Monitoring
Expect a wave of tools specialized in “LLM content ranking” — platforms that track which entities are cited across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews and others. The SEO tech stack will expand to include generative engine optimisation tools that map entity graphs to content performance.

6. Conversational Commerce and Richer UX
Search will blend into conversation: follow-ups, clarifications, and action triggers (book, buy, subscribe) will be native in AI flows. Brands that integrate transactional endpoints (APIs, commerce primitives, booking flows) into their entity profiles will capture direct ROI inside conversations.

7. Regulatory and Ethical Focus on Attribution
As models compile and present information, regulators and publishers will insist on clearer attribution, content provenance, and fairness. This could favor authoritative sources and penalize unverified scraping, shifting advantage to established brands that maintain data hygiene.

Bottom line: the LLM era won’t eliminate traditional SEO overnight, but it will redefine the rules. Entities win; keyword obsession loses. Organizations that proactively model their entities, create machine-readable value, and measure AI-centric KPIs will thrive.

## Conclusion

The entity revolution is not a future abstraction — it’s happening now. With 5.6% of U.S. desktop search traffic going to LLMs, 58.5% of Google searches resulting in zero clicks, and AI Overviews shaving 20–40% off organic CTRs (and up to 45% traffic erosion in some cases), the evidence is clear: traditional keyword-first SEO is being eroded by LLM-first discovery.

But this is an opportunity. Marketers who move from keyword obsession to entity strategy — treating brands, products, people and data as canonical entities with structured profiles, unique data and clear citations — will be favored by LLMs and AI overviews. Practical steps are straightforward: publish machine-readable entity data, break content into extractable, citable facts, invest in proprietary research, and track new metrics like AI mentions and citation accuracy.

Remember Patrick Coffee’s observation: chatbots are becoming the go-to source for many consumers. That doesn’t mean websites die; it means your role in the ecosystem changes. Be the authoritative entity the models cite. Build the data and content scaffolding that LLMs can trust. Measure impact on AI-driven discovery, not just SERP positions. And most importantly, start now — HubSpot finds 19% of marketers will adopt LLM SEO in 2025, leaving a broad runway for early movers to establish lasting entity authority.

Actionable recap:
- Implement JSON-LD schema for your core entities today.
- Produce one piece of original data or research quarterly.
- Convert your top informational pages into modular, citable blocks.
- Build an AI-mention monitoring dashboard and add AI KPIs to reporting.
- Treat entity governance as a cross-functional operational priority.

This is the new frontier of generative engine optimisation. The brands that treat entity-based SEO and AI search optimization as foundational capabilities will define visibility in the LLM-first future.
